_masks: [start_s, end_s, y_top, y_bottom]: hide the account usage notice at the start and the `ls -la` lines that show the local user name
phases: The human sends one message: a goal and two examples.
Intake: Sonnet checks herd status. It designs here; a Haiku builder will write the code.
herd init starts the task on its own branch, herd/slugify. Risk: medium.
Criteria: Sonnet writes the checks and tests before any slugify code.
Second look: herd design-brief makes Sonnet challenge its own reading of the request.
Red first: attacks are logged, then herd verify runs before any code: 0 of 6 pass.
Build: a Haiku herd-builder subagent writes the code in the background.
Stop gate: Herd blocks Sonnet from finishing early, 3 times, then lets it wait.
The builder runs the tests (13 pass) and herd verify (6 of 6).
Break it: Sonnet does not take the builder's word. It reads the diff itself.
It starts a fresh-context breaker subagent and probes the code too.
Found: invisible characters survive in slugs. A failing test, then the fix.
The breaker finds 4 more: ™, Ŀ, hooked letters and the Hawaiian okina.
New tests for them fail first.
Fixes them: 15 tests pass. Commits, then runs herd verify and herd done.
herd done: 6 of 6 criteria proven, with the commit and an evidence file.
Final report: what is proven and what is not, decisions and limits.
